title: The Read That Fails: Checksums, Retries and What a Bus Costs

questions.question: A bit is flipped on the wire and the driver has no check. What does the controller see?
options: A wrong number that looks like any other reading
questions.explanation: A flipped bit changes a value and nothing says so.

questions.question: What is the CRC-8 of the ASCII string 123456789 with polynomial 0x07 and start zero?
options: 0xF4, the standard figure to test an implementation against

questions.question: Why is a CRC better than a plain sum of the bytes?
options: It sees a change of order: on a five byte frame it missed 0 of 6 swapped pairs of bytes and a sum missed all 6
questions.explanation: A sum does not care about order.

questions.question: What should a bounded retry report beyond whether it worked?
options: How many attempts it took, and how many were timeouts and how many were bad frames, because those are different faults

questions.question: Each attempt fails with probability 0.28. What fraction of reads give up after 3 attempts?
A bus fails nine reads in ten. What does the arithmetic say?
options: It needs 44 attempts for 99 percent success, which means it needs fixing and not retrying
questions.explanation: A failure rate of one cannot be met by any number of attempts.
